newsitem.title: Malaysia: Malaysia Feb palm oil output seen down 11.8 pct-Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Feb palm oil output seen down 11.8 pct-Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in February is expected to fall by 11.8 percent to 509,000 tonnes from January, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Friday.
He had previously projected falls of 21 and 13 percent.
Wong put palm oil stocks at the end of February at 675,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 696,272 tonnes at end-January.

Wong said in a report the large decline was caused mainly by excessive rains. "Weather conditions had turned favourable throughout the country since the beginning of this month and a strong recovery in output is expected," said Wong.
Annual production growth in February and March also appears encouraging, he said, adding that the fall in CPO stocks occured mostly in East Malaysia because of the larger production shortfall.
Poor margins coupled with fewer working days had resulted in a marked cutback in palm oil and palm kernel olein exports in February compared to January, said Wong.
